description: On Tuesday, premiers from nine provinces signed a landmark agreement to implement direct-to-consumer alcohol sales, allowing Canadians to order alcohol directly from producers in participating provinces for personal consumption.
title: Alberta craft alcohol producers welcome direct-to-consumer deal

description: Experts have welcomed a new series of graphic images on cigarette packaging in Canada, which will be required by August 1, noting they lead to 'significant increases in the effectiveness' of health warnings.
title: Canada is rolling out new graphic image warnings on cigarette packs

description: Nine premiers across Canada have agreed it’s time to remove the trade barriers preventing people from buying alcohol from other provinces. Christine Fréchette says Quebec subscribes to the objectives of the agreement, but certain laws haven’t been amended that would allow it to come into force.
title: Why there’s hope Quebec will greenlight direct-to-consumer alcohol sales like other provinces have

description: Christopher Nolan's nearly three-hour epic The Odyssey was shot entirely using 70-mm Imax film — the first film in history to do so.
title: Only 9 Canadian cities can show you The Odyssey as it was filmed. Halifax is one

description: Saskatchewan Health Authority says hand hygiene is important for preventing hospital-acquired infections, but does not say why auditor's 2018 recommendations have yet to be fully implemented.
title: Regina hospitals still haven't cleaned up the hand-washing problem diagnosed in 2018

description: CBC Sports' daily newsletter looks at the Canadian track and field stars to watch at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland.
title: Commonwealth Games track and field preview: Men's relay team, hammer throw champs headline Canada's contenders

description: A First Nations-led wildfire evacuee centre in B.C. is taking steps to ensure survivors of intimate partner violence receive the unique support they need.
title: First Nations-led evacuation centre in B.C. ensures resources available for IPV survivors

description: Catherine Savoie was recently recruited to work at the Summerside Medical Centre. Her sister, Madeleine, is also there doing a two-year residency. Radio-Canada’s Laura Meader went to meet them.
title: There’s a new doctor in P.E.I. — and her twin sister is working here, too

description: Actor Michel Savard, slated to run in the Montreal electoral district of Gouin in the next election, has apologized for the Facebook comments, which he made before he became a Liberal candidate.
title: Quebec Liberals drop candidate who compared Parti Québécois to Nazis

description: Rebel News founder Ezra Levant told an Ottawa judge Wednesday that it would be his company’s "top priority" to ensure Tamara Lich complies with her court-ordered bail conditions if she is allowed to travel internationally as an employee of the right-wing media outlet.
title: Convoy leader Lich's bail conditions would be 'top priority' if travel allowed, Rebel News founder says

description: Harrington, Que., is approximately 40 kilometres from Mont-Tremblant, with a population of under 1,000 people. The probable tornado hit Tuesday afternoon, resulting in downed power lines and outages in the small municipality and other parts of the Laurentians.
title: Likely tornado tears through Harrington, Que., leaves behind major damage

description: Nadine Morin, a documentation specialist at the Anselme-Chiasson Centre for Acadian Studies at the Université de Moncton, said she's received genealogy requests from at least 30 people since January.
title: 'Lost Canadians' law opens door for U.S. descendants of Acadians to become citizens

description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says he would like to see his fellow premiers and Prime Minister Mark Carney be "a little more vocal" in the face of U.S. President Donald Trump's latest tariff threat.
title: Ford wants premiers, Carney to be 'more vocal' against Trump, says he 'can't do it alone'

description: Statistics Canada reports that both the rates and severity of crime were down almost across the board in 2025.
title: Crime rates dropped across most of the country in 2025: Statistics Canada

description: A Calgary judge has ruled that police can keep iPhones seized from former mayor Jyoti Gondek and former city councillor Sean Chu for up to a year. Police seized the devices in March as part of an investigation into allegations of municipal corruption.
title: Calgary police granted more time to search former mayor, councillor's phones in corruption investigation

description: A 33-year-old Toronto man is facing a terrorism charge for "public statements that advocated for the detestation and harm against members of the Israeli and Jewish communities," police say.
title: Terror charge laid against man accused of advocating harm against Jewish community at Toronto demonstrations

description: Ontario Emergency Preparedness Minister Jill Dunlop defended the province's wildfire response on CBC Radio's As It Happens on Tuesday, but her staff abruptly cut the interview short after she was asked to respond to criticism from community leaders.
title: Ontario emergency minister's interview cut short after wildfire response questions

description: Brewers in Prince Edward Island are applauding a move by nine provinces to drop barriers to the sale of alcohol among provinces. But they say it's ultimately unlikely to put more money in their pockets.
title: P.E.I. brewers say they won't see much return from provinces removing alcohol sale barriers

description: The Transportation Safety Board of Canada says it could not determine the exact cause of a freight train derailment in northern Quebec last December.
title: Federal agency links December train derailment in Quebec to temperature swings

description: Feeling lost when it comes to recent news about the Gordie Howe International Bridge? Earlier this month, Canada and the U.S. announced a fresh pact to open the bridge connecting Ontario and Michigan. There's also a 2012 deal that includes some toll revenue splitting. Here's what we know about how everything will work.
title: How does the new Gordie Howe bridge deal compare to the original one?

description: The emergency 911 service is currently down for all Manitoba communities except for Winnipeg, after the service went down at the dispatch centre in Brandon on Wednesday.
title: 911 outage affecting all of Manitoba outside of Winnipeg

description: A Swiss man who pleaded guilty to punching a protester in the face outside an Ottawa defence conference in 2024 was given an absolute discharge Wednesday before exiting the courtroom to angry shouts from supporters of the victim.
title: Swiss man who assaulted protester in Ottawa gets absolute discharge

description: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew says he's open to a west-east pipeline being pitched by his counterparts in Alberta and Ontario.
title: Manitoba 'willing to entertain' Alberta to Ontario pipeline: premier

description: A coalition of civil society groups is pushing back against criticism by a federal cabinet minister and Jewish organizations of an exhibit on Palestinian displacement at a national museum in Winnipeg.
title: Coalition calls on culture minister to withdraw criticism of human rights museum's Nakba exhibit

description: The company that owns the former General Motors site in St. Catharines, Ont., is challenging city orders to clean up building hazards found at the long-abandoned property, arguing the timeline to meet that order is "not reasonable".
title: Owners of abandoned former GM plants in St. Catharines, Ont., appeal orders to clean up hazards

description: Officials with School District 59 in northeastern B.C. say work is being done in stages over the summer and is expected to be complete this fall.
title: Work begins to tear down Tumbler Ridge Secondary School after deadly B.C. mass shooting

description: Some Indigenous leaders say they had a positive meeting with provincial and territorial leaders on the margins of this year's Council of the Federation gathering in Prince Edward Island, but issues remain with the list of invitees and Indigenous leaders' level of participation.
title: Some Indigenous leaders call premiers' meeting positive but inclusion remains an issue

description: Boats have been on the water of eastern Manitoba's Nutimik Lake since 6 a.m. Wednesday, marking the fifth day of searching for two boys believed to have drowned near Sturgeon Falls.
title: 'Just want them to come home': Family of 2 boys missing in Manitoba lake in pain, says lodge owner

description: It's rare that cancerous tumours can spread from one individual to another. But a genetic study suggests that's what's happening with melanoma skin cancer tumours among catfish in Quebec and the northeastern U.S.
title: Catfish in Quebec catch cancer from each other, study finds

description: Canada's premiers say they're behind the federal government as it tries to talk down U.S. President Donald Trump from his escalated trade war — although not everyone at the table is feeling confident that will happen soon.
title: Premiers rally behind Carney, but not everyone is confident a tariff deal is close

description: Ottawa has revealed the text of a controversial agreement with the U.S. to open the long-awaited Gordie Howe International Bridge near Windsor, Ont., which has been at the centre of recent political tensions.
title: Text of new Gordie Howe bridge deal seems to contradict Carney

description: Tom Molinski, 69, is relieved after receiving a cheque in the mail for nearly $24,000 from Manitoba Health after the province twice refused to reimburse him for an out-of-country spine surgery nearly two years ago.
title: Manitoba partially repays retiree for out-of-country surgery after twice refusing to pick up the tab

description: West Kelowna Mounties have issued an Amber Alert for a four-year-old boy. They say Atlas Andrews was last seen on Ridge Boulevard West in Kelowna at 11:20 a.m. Tuesday.
title: B.C. RCMP issue Amber Alert for 4-year-old boy

description: Teachers in Eskasoni First Nation are asking their school board to pause the use of facial recognition scanning that's being used to take teacher attendance, saying it's invading their privacy.
title: Teachers in N.S. First Nation say facial recognition technology puts their privacy at risk

description: Prices for fresh or frozen chicken thighs jumped 8.2 per cent from May to June — far above the monthly increases for the usual offenders like beef and coffee, according to inflation numbers.
title: Chicken thighs are how much? Here's what's driving the latest grocery sticker shock

description: Tamara Lich, a key figure in the 2022 convoy protest that paralyzed downtown Ottawa for nearly a month, is back in town Wednesday to ask a court for permission to travel internationally, including going on a Caribbean cruise and visiting the White House.
title: Convoy leader Tamara Lich asking court's permission to visit White House, go on cruise

description: Though last week's fatal black bear attack that killed a Saskatchewan couple came just months after another death involving a bear in the province, experts say such fatal attacks are still extremely rare.
title: Fatal black bear attacks are extremely rare despite recent killings in Saskatchewan, experts say

description: Wildfires that have torched huge areas of forest and devastated communities are also sending smoke far and wide, prompting air quality warnings in distant cities and heated political rhetoric from the U.S. Experts say there's nothing particularly unusual about this summer's smoke patterns — but they say wildfires are getting worse, and that's not likely to stop on either side of the border.
title: How wildfire smoke travels from Ontario to New York City — and turns distant city skies orange

description: Five years after Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc sent shockwaves around the world by announcing the First Nation found more than 200 possible unmarked graves at the site of the former Kamloops Indian Residential School, the chief says the community doesn't yet know if or when it will proceed with excavation.
title: Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc chief says probe into possible unmarked graves continues with no end in sight

description: U.S. President Donald Trump is imposing his new tariffs on Canadian exports under a section of law that has never been used since it was put on the books in 1930.
title: Trump's new tariffs on Canada could face a court challenge. But this time, he might win
